I've prepared the code without implementing the upcoming change. Here's what I did and why.

## What I changed

**Consolidated the three duplicate checks into a single seam.** In `addOwner`, the three separate `409 CONFLICT` conditionals (telephone, email, household) were inlined back-to-back. I replaced them with one call:

```java
if (isDuplicate(owner, ownerFieldsDto)) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
```

and extracted a private `isDuplicate(owner, ownerFieldsDto)` method (placed next to `isTelephoneInUse`/`isEmailInUse`/`isHouseholdInUse`) that composes the same three checks with identical logic and ordering.

## Why this is the right preparation

The upcoming change collapses all duplicate detection into one derived `identityKey` check. Landed directly against the current code, that author would have to surgically pick apart three interleaved conditionals inside an already-long `addOwner`. Now there is **one seam** — `isDuplicate` — whose body the change simply rewrites into the identity-key check, leaving `addOwner`'s orchestration untouched. The new `isIdentityInUse` slots in naturally as a sibling of the existing `is…InUse` methods (all sharing the `findAllOwners().stream()…anyMatch` idiom), and `Owner::getIdentityKey` slots in beside the existing `@Transient` derived getters (`getMembershipLevel`, `getContactPreference`).

## What I deliberately did *not* do

- **Not implemented the change**: the three sub-checks are preserved exactly, so two housemates with different telephones are still both rejected under the old rule — that behavior flip belongs to the change.
- **Did not switch household matching to `householdId`**: seed owners (`data.sql`) have no `household_id`, and the current check compares last name + address. Routing through the stored id would have silently changed behavior on seed data, so I left the comparison alone.
- **Left `Owner` untouched**: it already has the derived-getter pattern the new `getIdentityKey` will use, so no restructuring was warranted there.

## Verification

- `AcceptanceTest` (the identity-collision test): passing.
- Full `./mvnw test` suite: **BUILD SUCCESS**, 1 test run, 0 failures.
